evidence.quote: no conclusion in positive characteristic is asserted for an arbitrary regular sequence.

exclusions.query: Betti bounds for arbitrary regular sequences in positive characteristic
exclusions.reason: The arbitrary regular-sequence comparison is asserted only in characteristic zero.

hypotheses.statement: For every $n\ge1$, every ordered degree sequence $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n$, and every homogeneous ideal $I\subseteq\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ containing a regular sequence of these degrees, the spaces in [eq:prescription] exist and $J=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}J_d$ is a homogeneous ideal. For this single ideal, $$\beta^S_{p,j}(S/I)\le\beta^S_{p,j}(S/J) \qquad\text{for every \(p\ge0\) and \(j\in\mathbb Z\)}.$$ There is no restriction on the degrees or number of the additional generators of $I$.

Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $$S_F=F[x_1,\ldots,x_n],\qquad
 1\le c\le n,\qquad 2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_c,
 \qquad P_F=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c}),$$ with the standard grading and lexicographic order $x_1>\cdots>x_n$. Suppose that a homogeneous ideal $I\subseteq S_F$ contains a homogeneous regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ with $\deg f_i=a_i$. For $d\ge0$, put $$q_d=\dim_F I_d-\dim_F(P_F)_d.$$ This integer lies between zero and the number of degree-$d$ monomials outside $P_F$. Let $J_d$ be the sum of $(P_F)_d$ and the span of the $q_d$ lexicographically greatest such monomials. Then $J=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}J_d$ is a homogeneous ideal, and for this single ideal $$\dim_F(S_F/I)_d=\dim_F(S_F/J)_d\quad(d\ge0),\qquad
 \beta^{S_F}_{p,j}(S_F/I)\le\beta^{S_F}_{p,j}(S_F/J)
 \quad(p\ge0,\ j\in\mathbb Z).$$ There is no restriction on the degrees or number of the additional generators of $I$.

Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ be a homogeneous regular sequence in $\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, of degrees $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n$. There are a field extension $k/\mathbb C$, a central division $k$-algebra $\Delta$, and a commutative graded $k$-subalgebra $$k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\subseteq A\subseteq N=\Delta[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$$ generated by finitely many elements of degree one, containing $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in A_1$, such that $$\label{eq:triangular-forms}
 t_h^{a_h}=c_h f_h+\sum_{\ell<h}B_{h\ell}f_\ell
                  +\sum_{\ell>h}C_{h\ell}t_\ell
 \qquad(1\le h\le n).$$ Here $c_h\in k^\times$, $B_{h\ell},C_{h\ell}\in A$, and every summand has degree $a_h$. Moreover, $$\{t^\alpha=t_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots t_n^{\alpha_n}:
       \alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}^n\}$$ is a graded left-$\Delta$ basis of the *full* algebra $N$.

Every finitely generated graded $A$-module $B$ has a graded free resolution whose differentials have entries in $A_{>0}$. In such a resolution, the number of free generators of degree $j$ in homological position $p$ is $\beta^A_{p,j}(B)$. If $H\subsetneq A$ is a homogeneous ideal, then $$\beta^A_{p+1,j}(A/H)=\beta^A_{p,j}(H)
 \qquad(p\geq 0,\ j\in\mathbb Z).
 \label{filt:ideal-quotient}$$ If $H$ is monomial, a minimal resolution of $A/H$ can be chosen homogeneous for the exponent multigrading, with all generator multidegrees in $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^r$.

Let $K_\bullet(B)$ be the Koszul complex on $y_1,\ldots,y_r$ with coefficients in $B$. Its term of internal degree $j$ in position $p$ is $$K_p(B)_j=\bigoplus_{\substack{\sigma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}\\
                              |\sigma|=p}} B_{j-p}e_\sigma,$$ where $e_\sigma$ has degree $p$. Its homology satisfies $$\dim_F H_p(K_\bullet(B)_j)=\beta^A_{p,j}(B).$$

With $A,V,E,W$ and $\prec$ as above, for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, every $p\geq0$, and every $j\in\mathbb Z$ one has $$\begin{aligned} \dim_F(E/W)_d &=\dim_F(E/\operatorname{in}_{\prec}W)_d, \label{filt:hilbert}\\ \beta^A_{p,j}(E/W) &\leq\beta^A_{p,j}(E/\operatorname{in}_{\prec}W). \label{filt:betti} \end{aligned}$$

Let $S=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $k$ be a field containing $\mathbb C$, and let $\Delta$ be a finite-dimensional central division $k$-algebra. Put $m=\dim_k\Delta$ and $N=\Delta[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, where the $x_i$ are central. Suppose that $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in N_1$ commute and that $$N=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^n}\Delta t^\alpha
 \label{mono:basis}$$ is a graded direct-sum decomposition. Give $T=k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]$ a right action on $N$ by multiplication, $u\cdot y_i=ut_i$. For every homogeneous ideal $I\subseteq S$, the right $T$-module $Q=N/IN$ satisfies $$\begin{aligned}
 \dim_k Q_d&=m\dim_\mathbb C(S/I)_d
          &&(d\in\mathbb Z),\label{mono:dimension-transfer}\\
 \beta^T_{p,j}(Q)&=m\beta^S_{p,j}(S/I)
          &&(p\geq0,\ j\in\mathbb Z).
          \label{mono:betti-transfer}
\end{aligned}$$ Here right and left modules over the commutative ring $T$ are identified when computing $\mathop{\mathrm{Tor}}$.

Let $S=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $2\leq a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_n$, and let $I\subseteq S$ be a homogeneous ideal containing a homogeneous regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ with $\deg f_h=a_h$. Put $P=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_n^{a_n})$. There is a monomial ideal $M\subseteq S$ containing $P$ such that $$\begin{aligned}
 \dim_\mathbb C(S/M)_d&=\dim_\mathbb C(S/I)_d
                   &&(d\in\mathbb Z),\label{mono:hilbert-bound}\\
 \beta^S_{p,j}(S/I)&\leq\beta^S_{p,j}(S/M)
                   &&(p\geq0,\ j\in\mathbb Z).
                   \label{mono:betti-bound}
\end{aligned}$$

For every monomial ideal $K\subseteq S$, its vector-space image $D(K)$ is a homogeneous ideal. Moreover, $$\begin{gathered}
 \dim_\mathbb C(S/D(K))_d=\dim_\mathbb C(S/K)_d
 \quad(d\in\mathbb Z),\\
 \beta^S_{p,j}(S/D(K))=\beta^S_{p,j}(S/K)
 \quad(p\ge0,\ j\in\mathbb Z).
\end{gathered}$$ The map also satisfies $D(P)=P$.

Let $S=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n$, and put $P=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_n^{a_n})$. For every monomial ideal $K\supseteq P$, there is a monomial ideal $H\supseteq P$ stable in the box such that $$\dim_\mathbb C(S/H)_d=\dim_\mathbb C(S/K)_d\quad(d\in\mathbb Z)$$ and $$\beta^S_{p,j}(S/K)\le\beta^S_{p,j}(S/H)
 \qquad(p\ge0,\ j\in\mathbb Z).$$

Let $r\ge1$, let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be positive integers, and let $d\in\mathbb Z$. If $X\subseteq\mathcal B_r(d)$ is stable and $Y=\operatorname{Lex}(X)$, then $\partial Y$ is a lex segment and $$\label{box:three-inequalities}
 |\partial X|\ge|\partial Y|,
 \qquad |X(0)|\ge|Y(0)|,
 \qquad |X(b_r)|\le|Y(b_r)|.$$

Let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be positive integers, and let $H\subseteq\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ be a monomial ideal containing $P_r=(x_1^{b_1+1},\ldots,x_r^{b_r+1})$ and stable in the box sense. Then the subspace $\Lambda H$ defined in [box:lex-replacement] is a monomial ideal containing $P_r$. It is stable in the box sense and has the same Hilbert function as $H$.

For every $p\ge0$ and $j\in\mathbb Z$, the quantity $D^R_{p,j}(B)$ is the sum of the ranks of the two Koszul differentials adjacent to $K^R_p(B)_j$. If $U\subseteq B$ is a graded submodule and $V$ is a graded quotient of $B$, then $$D^R_{p,j}(U)\le D^R_{p,j}(B),\qquad
 D^R_{p,j}(V)\le D^R_{p,j}(B).$$ The quantity is additive on finite direct sums, satisfies $$D^R_{p,j}(B(-s))=D^R_{p,j-s}(B),$$ and vanishes when $R_{>0}B=0$.

Let $r\ge1$, let $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_r$, and let $A=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. Suppose that $H\subseteq A$ is a monomial ideal containing $(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_r^{a_r})$ and is stable in the box. Let $G=\Lambda H$ be its degreewise lex replacement inside the box, together with the prescribed pure powers. Then, for every $p\ge0$ and $j\in\mathbb Z$, $$\beta^A_{p,j}(H)\le\beta^A_{p,j}(G),
 \qquad
 \beta^A_{p,j}(A/H)\le\beta^A_{p,j}(A/G).$$

coverage.checked_domain: Every stable subset in every degree from -1 through sum(b)+1, for all bounds b in {1,2}^r and 1 <= r <= 3; includes arbitrary order of bounds, empty and full subsets.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact exhaustive bitmask enumeration with recursively generated bounded compositions; predecessor incidence checks shadows independently of successor construction.
